forces.title: Intensifying climate risks drive demand for financial risk data.
forces.description: The increasing frequency and severity of physical climate hazards are creating an urgent and growing demand for sophisticated catastrophe loss models and physical climate risk data. Financial institutions, including insurers and capital market participants, require these advanced tools for accurate underwriting, pricing, and capital allocation decisions to manage evolving climate-related financial stability issues.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

forces.title: Climate uncertainty reshapes financial risk modeling assumptions.
forces.description: Traditional actuarial methods, which assume stable probabilities of loss, are becoming less reliable due to climate change. The growing difficulty in predicting physical climate risk, coupled with increasing uncertainty from different climate pathways and inconsistent peril treatment, is forcing a fundamental shift in how financial risk is modeled and assessed. This requires new approaches and data.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

forces.title: Regulatory push for climate risk disclosure and data improvements.
forces.description: Prudential supervisors, including the Bank of England, are tightening regulatory frameworks around climate risk. This increasing regulatory scrutiny and the implementation of standards like ISSB-aligned reporting drive the need for improved climate risk data and sophisticated modelling tools. This creates a significant upside for financial data providers to support compliance and risk management.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

forces.title: Complexities hinder accurate climate risk data and model development.
forces.description: Despite growing demand, developing robust climate risk models faces significant challenges. These include difficulty downscaling global climate signals to local hazard changes, inconsistent treatment of secondary perils, and the influence of human factors on realized losses. These complexities increase uncertainty and pressure on financial data providers to develop more accurate and comprehensive solutions.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

forces.title: Need to quantify avoided losses for resilience investment data.
forces.description: Adaptation and resilience investments primarily generate value through avoided losses, which are challenging to quantify and reflect in traditional financial models. This creates a significant opportunity for financial data providers to develop new frameworks, methodologies, and data sets that can effectively measure and communicate the economic value of these protective benefits, bridging a critical financing gap.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

viewpoints.title: Climate risk intensity drives critical demand for advanced financial data and models.
viewpoints.description: TheCityUK's report highlights that escalating climate hazards are profoundly impacting insurability and broader financial markets. This situation mandates enhanced catastrophe loss and physical climate risk models for critical functions like underwriting, pricing, and capital allocation. The increasing uncertainty in projecting future losses, stemming from evolving climate patterns and intricate modeling challenges, necessitates substantial improvements in climate risk data and modeling capabilities. This growing, complex demand offers a cautious yet positive outlook for financial data and research providers to deliver essential tools that bolster capital markets stability and resilience financing.
viewpoints.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

demand_drivers.description: Rising frequency and severity of extreme weather events necessitate better risk assessment tools and data for financial institutions.
Pressure on insurance markets due to climate risk increases the demand for predictive models crucial for pricing, underwriting, and capital allocation.
Climate risks transmit into lending, investment, and asset valuations, requiring enhanced data and models to assess bankability and investability across the real economy.
Increasing regulatory focus on climate risk (e.g., from the Bank of England) mandates improved data and modelling for financial reporting and stress-testing requirements.

new_opportunities.description: Development of sophisticated catastrophe loss and physical climate risk models to address the evolving and complex nature of climate hazards.
Creating tools that translate global climate signals into local hazard changes and effectively address secondary and correlated perils for more precise risk assessment.
Developing frameworks and data to quantify the economic value of resilience investments and avoided losses, which are challenging to capture in traditional financial models.
Providing comprehensive data to align financial frameworks with long-term climate risk and resilience investment, overcoming biases towards short-term revenue generation.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Integrated Data Solutions for Financial Frameworks

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of the increasing and complex demand for climate-related risk assessment, modeling, and data to support underwriting, investment, lending, and regulatory compliance across financial markets due to intensifying physical climate risks.
market_sizing.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative
